scenario: Unary `-` on INT64_MIN wraps to INT64_MIN, per [LEXP.7.13.1] ('overflow wraps silently, two's complement') and [LEXP.7.10] (unary `-` is arithmetic negation on Int). Drives DS_RETE_UNOP_NEG in rete/eval.c, which routes through ds_i64_neg in int_ops.h, beside the add/sub/mul helpers that go through uint64_t: `-INT64_MIN` is UNDEFINED BEHAVIOUR in C, and an optimizer is entitled to assume the operand is never INT64_MIN. THE GUARD IS THE INSTRUMENT AND IT CANNOT PASS BY ACCIDENT: `-b.n == b.n` holds for only two int64 values, 0 and INT64_MIN, and the second rule pins that the fixture is testing the second -- a build where `-n` produced anything other than INT64_MIN fires neither. Sibling of LDET.6.3.1, which pins the same wrap for `+` rather than for unary `-`.
rules_ds:
schema Big scope logical:
    n: Int key

rule negation_wraps:
    Big b where -b.n == b.n
->
    log info "wrapped"

rule not_zero:
    Big b where b.n < 0
->
    log info "negative"
